rum.name: Web RUM
rum.description: Real user monitoring in the browser: page performance, frontend errors, resources and user sessions.

3.title: Upload production source maps
3.description: Upload the .map files under RUM settings → Source Maps & Symbols. The application ID, service and release must match the events exactly.
3.note: Do not use the RUM client token for uploads; uploading debug artifacts requires a signed-in user with stream configuration permission.

4.title: Verify an error event
4.description: Trigger a test error, then confirm the application, version and source location in the RUM error list.

rum-flutter.name: Flutter RUM
rum-flutter.description: Collect views, interactions, errors, resources, slow frames and session replay with the MoleSignal Flutter SDK.

2.title: Initialize and install the navigation observer

3.title: Generate Flutter AOT symbols
3.description: Keep the matching .symbols file for every release and architecture.

4.title: Upload and check the symbols
4.description: Under RUM settings → Source Maps & Symbols choose Flutter Symbols, enter the same application ID, service, release, platform and architecture, and upload each .symbols file.
4.note: Production stacks from the current SDK still need the relative addresses and build identifiers from the Flutter SDK fix list below before they resolve AOT symbols reliably.

5.title: Verify sessions and errors
5.description: Run a release build and trigger a test exception; confirm the RUM session, error and replay belong to this application.

rum-android.name: Android RUM
rum-android.description: Native Android apps report sessions and errors over the RUM HTTP protocol, with R8 and NDK stack restoration.

1.title: Integrate the RUM HTTP protocol
1.description: Until the native Android SDK ships, integrate through your existing network layer. Errors are shown below; sessions, actions and replay go to /api/v1/rum/sessions, /api/v1/rum/actions and /api/v1/rum/replay, and must use the same application ID.

2.title: Keep the R8 mapping.txt
2.description: After a release build, save app/build/outputs/mapping/release/mapping.txt; it changes with every release.

3.title: Keep unstripped NDK symbols
3.description: With C/C++ code, keep the unstripped .so for each ABI. You may gzip them before upload, but do not upload only the stripped .so files from the APK.

4.title: Report NDK frame addresses
4.description: Native crash frames must carry the module, instruction address, image load address and Build ID; the server converts them to module-relative addresses.

5.title: Upload Android debug artifacts
5.description: Under RUM settings → Source Maps & Symbols upload the Android mapping.txt and the Android Native Symbols separately, with the application ID, version, ABI and Build ID.

6.title: Verify the deobfuscated stack
6.description: Trigger a test exception from a release build and confirm class names, method names and source lines are restored.

rum-ios.name: iOS RUM
rum-ios.description: Native iOS apps report error addresses over the RUM HTTP protocol and restore functions and source locations with dSYM.

1.title: Integrate the RUM HTTP protocol
1.description: Until the native iOS SDK ships, integrate through URLSession. Errors are shown below; sessions, actions and replay go to /api/v1/rum/sessions, /api/v1/rum/actions and /api/v1/rum/replay, and must use the same application ID.

2.title: Archive and keep the dSYM
2.description: Keep the .xcarchive after Xcode Archive; the app binary and the dSYM must have the same UUID.

3.title: Upload the dSYM DWARF file
3.description: Under RUM settings → Source Maps & Symbols choose Apple dSYM, upload the Contents/Resources/DWARF/<AppName> file from the dSYM bundle (or its .gz) and enter the UUID.

4.title: Verify the release stack
4.description: Trigger a test error from a TestFlight or release device build and confirm functions, files and line numbers are restored.

continuous-profiling.name: Continuous profiling
continuous-profiling.description: Continuous profiling (flame graphs) through OTLP Profiles, Pyroscope or direct pprof upload, to locate CPU, memory and lock contention.

1.title: OTLP Profiles (OpenTelemetry)
1.description: Point the OTel eBPF profiler or SDK at the built-in OTLP profiles endpoint (Alpha).

2.title: Pyroscope SDK
2.description: An existing Pyroscope agent can talk to the compatible intake endpoint directly (format=pprof|folded|lines).

3.title: Raw pprof upload
3.description: Upload a gzip-compressed pprof directly (from runtime/pprof, for example), or use the upload button at the top right of the Profiles page.

curl.name: curl (raw JSON)
curl.description: The simplest way: HTTP POST a JSON array to the intake endpoint.

bulk-ndjson.name: Bulk NDJSON
bulk-ndjson.description: Bulk push through the Elasticsearch-compatible _bulk API, or a JSON array straight to the native intake.

1.title: Elasticsearch-compatible _bulk
1.description: Action and document lines alternate (NDJSON); _index selects the target stream, falling back to the stream-name header or default.

2.title: Native bulk (JSON array)
2.description: When the ES format is not needed, POST a JSON array to the intake endpoint, up to 5 MB per request.

opentelemetry.name: OpenTelemetry
opentelemetry.description: OpenTelemetry SDKs and applications send OTLP/HTTP directly; logs, metrics and traces arrive through one integration.

1.title: OTLP/HTTP endpoint
1.description: Set the endpoint to /api; the SDK appends /v1/{signal} (→ /api/v1/traces and so on). The optional stream-name header selects the target stream.

3.title: OTLP gRPC (:4317)
3.description: OTLP gRPC always listens on :4317; the [otlp_grpc] section changes the listen address, port and message size.
3.note: Exposed port: in production, put TLS and firewall rules in front of :4317.

otel-collector.name: OTel Collector
otel-collector.description: Relay logs, metrics and traces to MoleSignal through the OpenTelemetry Collector's otlphttp exporter.

1.title: Collector configuration (otlphttp exporter)
1.description: The Collector forwards over OTLP/HTTP: set the endpoint to /api and /v1/{signal} is appended automatically.

2.title: Collector configuration (otlp gRPC exporter, :4317)
2.description: Use the built-in OTLP gRPC (:4317) instead. Add tls.insecure: true for plaintext connections and remove it when going through TLS in production.
